questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A series $L-C-R$ circuit is connected to a variable frequency ac source of voltage amplitude $20\text{ V}$. The maximum current amplitude in the circuit is $2\text{ A}$. The angular frequencies at which the current amplitude drops to $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ of its maximum value are $95\text{ rad s}^{-1}$ and $105\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. The Quality factor ($Q$) of the circuit and the voltage amplitude across the inductor at resonance are respectively:
questions.solution:
The resonant angular frequency $\omega_0$ is the average of the half-power frequencies:

$\omega_0 = \dfrac{95 + 105}{2} = 100\text{ rad s}^{-1}$

The bandwidth $\Delta \omega$ is the difference between the half-power frequencies:

$\Delta \omega = 105 - 95 = 10\text{ rad s}^{-1}$

The Quality factor $Q$ is given by:

$Q = \dfrac{\omega_0}{\Delta \omega} = \dfrac{100}{10} = 10$

At resonance, the voltage amplitude across the inductor $V_L$ is $Q$ times the source voltage amplitude:

$V_L = Q \times V_{\text{source}} = 10 \times 20\text{ V} = 200\text{ V}$

Answer: $10$ and $200\text{ V}$

questions.q: An AC source of variable frequency is connected in series with a light bulb and an ideal inductor. If the frequency of the AC source is gradually increased while keeping the voltage amplitude constant, what happens to the inductive reactance and the brightness of the bulb?
options: Inductive reactance decreases and the brightness of the bulb increases.
Inductive reactance increases and the brightness of the bulb increases.
Inductive reactance increases and the brightness of the bulb remains constant.
Inductive reactance increases and the brightness of the bulb decreases.
questions.solution:
The inductive reactance of an ideal inductor is given by $X_L = 2\pi f L$, where $f$ is the frequency of the AC source.

As the frequency $f$ increases, the inductive reactance $X_L$ increases.

The total impedance of the series circuit is $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}$, where $R$ is the resistance of the bulb. An increase in $X_L$ leads to an increase in the total impedance $Z$.

Since the voltage amplitude is constant, the RMS current in the circuit $I_{rms} = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{Z}$ will decrease.

The brightness of the bulb depends on the power dissipated by it, which is given by $P = I_{rms}^2 R$. Since the current decreases, the power dissipated decreases, and hence the brightness of the bulb decreases.

Answer: Inductive reactance increases and the brightness of the bulb decreases.

questions.q: A coil is connected to a $12\text{ V}$ DC source and draws a steady current of $4\text{ A}$. When the same coil is connected to an AC source of $12\text{ V}$ (rms) and angular frequency $50\text{ rad/s}$, the rms current in the circuit is $2.4\text{ A}$. The inductance of the coil is:
questions.solution:
When the coil is connected to a DC source, the inductive reactance is zero. The resistance $R$ of the coil is:
$R = \dfrac{V_{DC}}{I_{DC}} = \dfrac{12}{4} = 3\ \Omega$

When connected to an AC source, the net impedance $Z$ of the coil is:
$Z = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}} = \dfrac{12}{2.4} = 5\ \Omega$

The impedance of the coil (which acts as a series LR circuit) is given by:
$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}$
$5 = \sqrt{3^2 + X_L^2}$
$25 = 9 + X_L^2 \Rightarrow X_L^2 = 16 \Rightarrow X_L = 4\ \Omega$

The inductive reactance is $X_L = \omega L$. Substituting the given values:
$4 = 50 \times L$
$L = \dfrac{4}{50}\text{ H} = 0.08\text{ H} = 80\text{ mH}$

Answer: $80\text{ mH}$

questions.q: A series LCR circuit has a resonant frequency $f_0$. If the inductance of the circuit is doubled and the capacitance is reduced to one-eighth of its original value, the new resonant frequency of the circuit will be :
questions.solution:
The initial resonant frequency of the series LCR circuit is given by:

$f_0 = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$

When the inductance is doubled ($L' = 2L$) and the capacitance is reduced to one-eighth ($C' = \dfrac{C}{8}$), the new resonant frequency $f'$ is:

$f' = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{L'C'}}$

Substituting the new values:

$f' = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{2L \times \dfrac{C}{8}}}$

$f' = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{LC}{4}}}$

$f' = \dfrac{2}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$

$f' = 2f_0$

Thus, the new resonant frequency is $2f_0$.

Answer: $2f_0$

For an AC circuit, the capacitive reactance is given by:

For a DC circuit, the frequency $f = 0$.
$X_{C2} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi (0) C} = \infty$ (infinity)

Thus, a capacitor blocks DC and offers infinite reactance.
The correct values are $100 \, \Omega$ and infinity.

Answer: $100 \, \Omega$, infinity

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a purely capacitive AC circuit, if the frequency of the source is doubled, the peak displacement current between the capacitor plates is also doubled.
Reason (R): The capacitive reactance of a capacitor is inversely proportional to the frequency of the AC source.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct.
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
The capacitive reactance is given by $X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi f C}$. This shows that $X_C$ is inversely proportional to the frequency $f$ of the AC source. Thus, Reason (R) is correct.

The peak conduction current in the circuit is $I_m = \dfrac{V_m}{X_C} = V_m (2\pi f C)$. This means the current is directly proportional to the frequency ($I_m \propto f$).

According to Maxwell's equations, the displacement current between the capacitor plates is equal to the conduction current in the connecting wires. Therefore, if the frequency $f$ is doubled, the peak displacement current is also doubled. Thus, Assertion (A) is correct.

Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A) because the inverse proportionality of reactance to frequency is the underlying cause for the direct proportionality of current to frequency.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An alternating current has a frequency of $50$ Hz. What is the shortest time it takes for the current to reach its root mean square (RMS) value, starting from zero?
questions.solution:
The instantaneous value of an alternating current is given by $I = I_0 \sin(2\pi f t)$.

The RMS value of the current is $I_{rms} = \dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$.

To find the time taken to reach the RMS value from zero, we set $I = I_{rms}$:

$I_0 \sin(2\pi f t) = \dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\sin(2\pi f t) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

The shortest time corresponds to the smallest positive phase angle, which is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ radians.

$2\pi f t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$t = \dfrac{1}{8f}$

Given $f = 50$ Hz:

$t = \dfrac{1}{8 \times 50} = \dfrac{1}{400}$ s.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{400}$ s

$t = \dfrac{1}{8f}$

Given $f = 50$ Hz:

$t = \dfrac{1}{8 \times 50} = \dfrac{1}{400}$ s.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{400}$ s

questions.q:
A series LCR circuit with inductance $L = 0.1\text{ H}$ and capacitance $C = 10\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ is connected across various voltage sources. Match the voltage sources in List-I with the corresponding steady-state behavior of the circuit in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) $V = V_0 \sin(1000t)$(I) Current leads the voltage
(B) $V = V_0 \sin(500t)$(II) Current lags the voltage
(C) $V = V_0 \sin(2000t)$(III) Current is in phase with the voltage
(D) $10\text{ V}$ DC source(IV) Steady state current is zero

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The resonant angular frequency of the LCR circuit is:
$\omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{0.1 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}}} = 1000\text{ rad s}^{-1}$

(A) For $V = V_0 \sin(1000t)$, $\omega = 1000\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. Since $\omega = \omega_0$, the circuit is at resonance and the current is in phase with the voltage. (A) matches with (III).

(B) For $V = V_0 \sin(500t)$, $\omega = 500\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. Since $\omega < \omega_0$, capacitive reactance $X_C$ is greater than inductive reactance $X_L$. The circuit is capacitive, so the current leads the voltage. (B) matches with (I).

(C) For $V = V_0 \sin(2000t)$, $\omega = 2000\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. Since $\omega > \omega_0$, inductive reactance $X_L$ is greater than capacitive reactance $X_C$. The circuit is inductive, so the current lags the voltage. (C) matches with (II).

(D) For a $10\text{ V}$ DC source, $\omega = 0$. The capacitor offers infinite reactance ($X_C = \infty$) and blocks direct current, so the steady state current is zero. (D) matches with (IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An AC voltage $V = 100\sqrt{2} \sin(100 t)$ Volts is applied to a series LCR circuit with $R = 40 \, \Omega$, $L = 0.7$ H, and $C = 250 \, \mu$F. The average power dissipated in the circuit is :
questions.solution:
From the voltage equation $V = 100\sqrt{2} \sin(100 t)$, the peak voltage is $V_m = 100\sqrt{2}$ V and the angular frequency is $\omega = 100$ rad/s.

The RMS voltage is $V_{rms} = \dfrac{V_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{100\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 100$ V.

The inductive reactance is $X_L = \omega L = 100 \times 0.7 = 70 \, \Omega$.

The capacitive reactance is $X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{100 \times 250 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{1}{25 \times 10^{-3}} = 40 \, \Omega$.

The impedance of the circuit is $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = \sqrt{40^2 + (70 - 40)^2} = \sqrt{40^2 + 30^2} = 50 \, \Omega$.

The RMS current in the circuit is $I_{rms} = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{Z} = \dfrac{100}{50} = 2$ A.

The average power dissipated is $P = I_{rms}^2 R = (2)^2 \times 40 = 4 \times 40 = 160$ W.

Answer: $160$ W

questions.q: In a damped $LC$ circuit, the amplitude of the oscillating charge decreases exponentially. If the charge amplitude drops to $\dfrac{1}{e}$ of its initial value in $5 \text{ ms}$ and the inductance of the circuit is $20 \text{ mH}$, the resistance of the circuit is:
questions.solution:
The amplitude of charge in a damped $LC$ circuit varies with time as:
$Q = Q_0 e^{-\dfrac{Rt}{2L}}$

The charge amplitude drops to $\dfrac{1}{e}$ of its initial value when the exponent is $-1$.
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{Rt}{2L} = 1$

Rearranging for resistance $R$:
$R = \dfrac{2L}{t}$

Given $L = 20 \text{ mH} = 20 \times 10^{-3} \text{ H}$ and $t = 5 \text{ ms} = 5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s}$:
$R = \dfrac{2 \times 20 \times 10^{-3}}{5 \times 10^{-3}} = \dfrac{40}{5} = 8 \ \Omega$

Answer: $8 \ \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An alternating current given by $I = I_0 \sin \omega t$ flows through a purely inductive circuit of inductance $L$. Which of the following expressions represents the instantaneous power $P$ supplied to the inductor by the source?
questions.solution:
The voltage across a pure inductor is given by $V = L \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.

Given $I = I_0 \sin \omega t$, we have:
$V = L \dfrac{d}{dt}(I_0 \sin \omega t) = \omega L I_0 \cos \omega t$

The instantaneous power $P$ is the product of instantaneous voltage and current:
$P = V \times I = (\omega L I_0 \cos \omega t)(I_0 \sin \omega t)$

Using the trigonometric identity $2 \sin \theta \cos \theta = \sin 2\theta$, we get:
$P = \dfrac{1}{2} \omega L I_0^2 (2 \sin \omega t \cos \omega t) = \dfrac{1}{2} \omega L I_0^2 \sin 2\omega t$

Note that while the average power over a complete cycle is zero, the instantaneous power varies sinusoidally with twice the frequency of the source.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2} \omega L I_0^2 \sin 2\omega t$

questions.q: A series LCR circuit with inductance $2 \text{ H}$ and resistance $10 \text{ \Omega}$ is connected to an AC source of voltage $V = 200 \sin(100t)$ volt. If the current and voltage in the circuit are in phase, the value of capacitance and the impedance of the circuit are respectively:
questions.solution:
From the given voltage equation $V = 200 \sin(100t)$, the angular frequency of the source is $\omega = 100 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

Since the current and voltage are in phase, the circuit is in resonance. At resonance, the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance ($\omega L = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$).

$\Rightarrow C = \dfrac{1}{\omega^2 L} = \dfrac{1}{(100)^2 \times 2} = \dfrac{1}{20000} \text{ F}$

$\Rightarrow C = 50 \times 10^{-6} \text{ F} = 50 \text{ \mu F}$

At resonance, the impedance of the circuit is purely resistive and is equal to the resistance $R$.

$\Rightarrow Z = R = 10 \text{ \Omega}$

Answer: $50 \text{ \mu F}, 10 \text{ \Omega}$

questions.q:
An alternating voltage given by the equation $v(t) = 200 \sin(100t)$ is applied across a pure capacitor of capacitance $50 \mu\text{F}$. The corresponding time-domain equation for the current $i(t)$ in the circuit is:
(Assume $v(t)$ is in volts, $i(t)$ is in amperes, and $t$ is in seconds)
questions.solution:
Comparing the given voltage equation $v(t) = 200 \sin(100t)$ with the standard form $v(t) = V_0 \sin(\omega t)$, we get:
Peak voltage, $V_0 = 200$ V
Angular frequency, $\omega = 100$ rad/s

The capacitive reactance is:
$X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{100 \times 50 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{1}{5 \times 10^{-3}} = 200 \Omega$

The peak current is:
$I_0 = \dfrac{V_0}{X_C} = \dfrac{200}{200} = 1.0$ A

In a purely capacitive circuit, the current leads the voltage by a phase angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Therefore, the equation for the current is:
$i(t) = I_0 \sin(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}) = 1.0 \sin(100t + \dfrac{\pi}{2})$

Answer: $i(t) = 1.0 \sin(100t + \dfrac{\pi}{2})$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A series combination of resistor $(R)$ and capacitor $(C)$ is connected to an AC source of angular frequency $\omega$. Keeping the voltage same, if the frequency is changed to $\frac{\omega}{3}$, the current becomes half of the original current. Then the ratio of the capacitive reactance and resistance at the former frequency is
questions.solution:
In the first case, capacitive reactance,
$X_C=\frac{1}{\omega C}$
Impedance of the circuit, $Z=\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}$
Current in the circuit, $I=\frac{V}{Z}=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}} \ldots$ (i)
In the second case, $\omega^{\prime}=\frac{\omega}{3} \therefore \quad$ Capacitive reactance,
$X_C^{\prime}=\frac{1}{\omega^{\prime} C}=\frac{1}{\frac{\omega}{3} C}=\frac{3}{\omega C}=3 X_C$
Impedance of the circuit,
$Z^{\prime}=\sqrt{R^2+X_C^{\prime 2}}=\sqrt{R^2+9 X_C^2}$
Current in the circuit,
$\frac{I}{2}=\frac{V}{Z^{\prime}}=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2+9 X_C^2}}$
Divide (ii) by (i), we get
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}}{\sqrt{R^2+9 X_C^2}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4}=\frac{R^2+X_C^2}{R^2+9 X_C^2} \\ & 5 X_C^2=3 R^2 \text{$ or $} \frac{X_C}{R}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}}=\sqrt{0.6}\end{aligned}$

Reason : At resonance, in LCR series circuit, the current and e.m.f are not in phase with each other.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
At resonance X_L=X_C or $\omega L=\frac{1}{\omega C}$.
Because of this impedance of $L C R$ series
circuit become equal to resistance of circuit
$\left(Z=\sqrt{R^2+\left(X_L-X_C\right)^2}$\right)$.
Therefore from $I=$\frac{E}{Z}=\frac{E}{R}$, at resonance, current in LCR series circuit is maximum. Correspondingly phase angle is also equal to zero. Therefore emf and current are in phase in L C R series circuit.

questions.q: In an $A C$ circuit, voltage $V=V_0 \sin \omega t$ and inductor $L$ is connected across the circuit. Then the instantaneous power will be
questions.solution:
If $\frac{d I}{d t}$ is the rate of change of current through inductor $L$ of any instant, then induced emf in the inductor of the same instant is $=\left(-\frac{L d I}{d t}\right)$ To maintain the flow of current in the circuit applied voltage must be equal and opposite to the induced voltage. $\therefore \quad V=-\left(-L \frac{d I}{d t}\right) \Subset$ Given, $V=V_0 \sin \omega t$
$\therefore \quad V_0 \sin \omega t=\frac{L d I}{d t}$ $\frac{d I}{d t}=\frac{V_0}{L} \sin \omega t$ or $I=\frac{-V_0}{L} \frac{\cos \omega t}{\omega}$
Instantaneous power, $\because \quad P=V I$ $=\left(V_0 \sin \omega t\right)\left(-\frac{V_0 \cos \omega t}{L \omega}\right) \quad(\mathrm{Using}$ (i) \& (ii)) $=\frac{-V_0^2 \sin 2 \omega t}{2 L \omega}$

Instantaneous power, $\because \quad P=V I$ $=\left(V_0 \sin \omega t\right)\left(-\frac{V_0 \cos \omega t}{L \omega}\right) \quad(\mathrm{Using}$ (i) \& (ii)) $=\frac{-V_0^2 \sin 2 \omega t}{2 L \omega}$

questions.q:
Assertion : We use a thick wire in the secondary of a step down transformer to reduce the production heat.
Reason : When the plane of the armature is parallel to the line of force of magnetic field, the magnitude of induced e.m.f. is maximum.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: A step-down transformer converts electrical energy from a high voltage to one at a low voltage. Accordingly the current in the secondary will be larger than that in the primary. In order to produce less heat in the secondary, we use a wire of lesser resistance i.e. thick wire. We also know that when the plane of the armature is parallel to the lines of force of magnetic field, the rate of change of magnetic flux linked with it is maximum. Therefore the e.m.f. induced in the armature in this orientation is maximum.

Given, $R=100 \Omega, V=200 \mathrm{~V}, \theta=60^{\circ}, \omega=300 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
$\therefore$ Phase angle, $\tan \theta=\frac{X_L}{R}=\frac{X_C}{R}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \tan 60^{\circ}=\frac{X_L}{R}=\frac{X_C}{R}$
$\therefore \quad X_L=X_C=\sqrt{3} R$
i.e.
$Z=\sqrt{R^2+(\sqrt{3} R-\sqrt{3} R)^2}=R$
So average power,
$P=\frac{V^2}{R}=\frac{200 \times 200}{100}=400 \mathrm{~W}$

questions.q: An inductor $(L=20 \mathrm{H})$, a resistor $(R=100 \Omega)$ and a battery $(E=10 \mathrm{~V})$ are connected in series. After a long time, the circuit is short-circuited and then the battery is disconnected. Find the current in the circuit at 1 ms after short circuiting.
questions.solution:
The initial current $i=i_0=\frac{E}{R}=\frac{10}{100} =0.10 \mathrm{~A}$
the time constant, $\tau=\frac{L}{R}=\frac{20 \mathrm{mH}}{100 \Omega} =0.20 \mathrm{~ms}$
The current at $t=1 \mathrm{~ms}$ is
$\begin{aligned} i & =i_0 e^{-t / \tau} \\ & =(0.10) e^{\left(\frac{-1 \mathrm{~ms}}{0.20 \mathrm{~ms}}\right)} \\ & =(0.10) e^5=6.7 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A choke is preferred to a resistance for limiting current in AC circuit because
options: there is no wastage of power
choke is a good absorber of heat
questions.solution:
In an AC circuit, the coil of high inductance and negligible resistance used to control current, is called the choke coil. The power factor of such a coil is given by
$\cos \phi=\frac{R}{\sqrt{R^2+\omega^2 L^2}}$
$=\frac{R}{\omega L} \quad($ as $R \ll \lt \omega L)$
As $R \ll \omega L, \cos \phi$ is very small. Thus, the power absorbed by the coil is very small. The only loss of energy is due to hysteresis in the iron core, which is much less than the loss of energy in the resistance that can also reduce the current if placed instead of the choke coil.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When power is drawn from the secondary coil of the transformer, the dynamic resistance
questions.solution: When the secondary coil circuit is open, the magnetic flux in the core is produced by the primary current only. When the secondary circuit is closed, the currents in the secondary coil also produce magnetic flux in the core but in opposite direction. This decreases the core flux and hence reduces the back emf produced in the primary coil. The source emf is now in excess of the back emf, more current is drawn in the primary coil. Hence, power factor is no longer zero. The power factor has increased or the phase difference is no longer $90^{\circ}$, ie, phase difference has decreased. Thus, dynamic resistance has increased.

questions.question: In a $L-C-R$ circuit, the capacitance is made one-fourth, then what should be change in inductance, so that the circuit remains in resonance?
questions.explanation:
Resonance frequency $f=\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{L C}}$
For the circuit to remain in resonance, $\sqrt{L C}=$ constant
$\begin{aligned}$ or $\quad L_1 C_1 & =L_2 C_2 \\ or \quad L C & =L_2 \frac{C}{4} \\ \therefore L_2 & =4 L\end{aligned} \therefore$ Inductance should be change to four times.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An L.C. circuit is in the state of resonance. If $C=0.1 \mu \mathrm{F}$ and $L=0.25$ Henry. Neglecting ohmic resistance of circuit. What is the frequency of oscillations?
questions.solution:
From the formula, the frequency of oscillation is
$\begin{aligned} f & =\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{L C}} \\ & =\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{0.25 \times 0.1 \times 10^{-6}}} \\ & =1007 \mathrm{~Hz}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transmitting station transmits radiowaves of wavelength 360 m . Calculate the inductance of coil required with a condenser of capacity $1.20 \mu \mathrm{F}$ in the resonant circuit to receive them
questions.solution:
The frequency of radiowaves (speed $c=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} ) transmitted
$f=$\frac{c}{\lambda}=\frac{3 \times 10^8}{360}=$8.3 \times 10^5 $\mathrm{~Hz}$
Frequency of series resonant circuit
$\begin{aligned}f & =\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{L C}} \\\text{ or } \quad L & =\frac{1}{(2 \pi f)^2 C}\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{\left(2 \times 3.14 \times 8.3 \times 10^5\right)^2 \times 1.20 \times 10^{-6}} \\ & =3.07 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{H}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The peak value of alternating current is $5 \sqrt{2}$ ampere. The mean square value of current will be
questions.solution:
Here: $I_0=5 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~A}$
Root mean square value of current
$I_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}=5 \mathrm{~A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A lamp in which 10 amp current can flow at 15 V, is connected with an alternating source of potential 220 V. The frequency of source is 50 Hz. The inductance of choke coil required to light the bulb is
questions.solution:
The resistance of lamp
$R=\frac{V}{I}=\frac{15}{10}=1.5 \Omega$
The impedance of circuit
$Z=\frac{V}{I}=\frac{220}{10}=22 \mathrm{ohm}$
Again impedance $Z=\sqrt{R^2+\omega^2 L^2}$
or $\quad 22=\sqrt{(1.5)^2+(2 \times \pi \times 50)^2 L^2}$
or $\quad(22)^2=(1.5)^2+4 \pi^2 \times 50^2 \times L^2$
or $\quad L=0.07$ Henry
